newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cash-mad Hong Kong sells 1997-anything as history.
newsitem.headline: Cash-mad Hong Kong sells 1997-anything as history.

text.p: Whatever 1997 means to you, it spells big money to collectors marking Hong Kong's transition to China.
Almost anything to do with the number 1997 is marketable because the year is a landmark in Chinese history.
Special edition newspapers will sell at book prices and unique car licence-plates exceed the value of even luxury cars.
The ranks of 1997 money-generators are rapidly swelling 11 days before the territory begins a new era of Chinese rule after 156 years of British colonialism.
The Beijing-backed newspaper Wen Wei Po says it will issue 1997 copies of a special edition on July 1, printed on glossy paper with a gold-embossed hard cover, selling at HK$1,000 (US$130) each.
This is a whopping 200 times the standard price of HK$5.
In China, one of Shanghai's major newspapers Wen Hui Daily said it will print a limited edition on coloured silk on that day, selling it for 5,000 yuan (US$600).
A collector of six car plates bearing the magic 1, 9, 9, 7, numbers is asking for a total of HK$3 million, the Hong Kong Standard said.
This, in a wealthy city of 6.4 million with the world's highest ratios of top-brand luxury cars.
Such plates, carrying combinations of the numbers HK1997 and BJ1997 (Beijing 1997), often command astronomical prices among some superstitious bidders.
Auctioneers withdrew a HK1997 plate in January after bidders failed to reach the target price of HK$4.8 million.

At any time, other wildly-sought numbers are eight, which rhymes with "prosperity" in Chinese, and two, which sounds the same as "ease" in Cantonese, the dialect spoken in the southern province and Hong Kong. "Death" has a similar sound to four, the most dreaded number.
A wine company said it is launching the "Official 1997 Wines", a trio of red, white and sparkling.
Remy China and Hong Kong Ltd will sell the three Chinese wines on June 25. A company spokesman said the wines are not of the 1997 vintage, as harvest takes place in autumn.
But imbibers are clearly poised to greet the handover in good spirits, anyway.
